# Utilities whose corpus does not yet pass on Darwin.
#
# The macOS lane runs the WHOLE catalogue and compares the set of test
# functions that failed against this list. A name that fails and is not here
# fails the lane — that is the ratchet, and it is what stops the Darwin
# result from drifting while the divergences are worked through.
#
# Entries only ever LEAVE. When a utility's Darwin branch lands, its line is
# deleted in the same change, and the lane starts holding it to GNU from then
# on. Nothing is ever added to buy a green lane: a new name here means a
# utility that used to pass on Darwin now does not, which is a regression to
# fix rather than to record.
#
# The one exception was finishing the seed, below, and it is not a precedent.
#
# One test function per line, so the granularity is a utility rather than a
# case. The case counts behind these names, and the clusters they fall into,
# are in #9714; the largest by far is the listing code behind vdir, ls and
# dir, which is one program and 43% of the failures.
#
# Seeded from what was believed to be the first complete run of the catalogue
# on macos-15 — 1411 failures over 14814 tests (PR #9676) — and it was not
# complete. That round stopped after `ptx_test.go`: its failing set is a clean
# alphabetical prefix by test FILE, and the one name in it that looks like an
# exception, TestVdir, is declared in `ls_test.go`. Everything from
# `pwd_test.go` onward never executed, so 32 utilities went unmeasured and
# unlisted.
#
# The round completes now — 19909 tests in 264s against that round's 14814 in
# 648s — because #9738 capped a case that could write about 10^20 bytes and
# fixed another that recursively chmod'd /private for 37 seconds a run. With
# the catalogue finishing, those 32 names appeared at once and the ratchet read
# them as 32 simultaneous regressions, which held `main` red and cancelled
# every lane behind it.
#
# They are not regressions: they are the tail of the seed. Verified by
# comparing the failing set of the seed round's own job log against `main`'s —
# the difference is exactly the names from `pwd_test.go` on, and the set is
# identical on `main` and on an unrelated branch. The case counts behind all
# 83 are #9714's.
